title: Iran Submits Revised 14-Point Peace Proposal to US via Pakistan
detail: Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed it submitted a revised 14-point peace proposal to the United States through Pakistan serving as intermediary, after the US rejected a previous version of Iran's plan. The new proposal's key demands included: resolution of all issues within 30 days, an end to the US-Israeli naval blockade, withdrawal of US forces from Iran's geographic periphery, release of all frozen Iranian assets, war reparations, comprehensive lifting of sanctions, and a new jointly-negotiated mechanism governing the Strait of Hormuz. Iran emphasized it was willing to discuss the nuclear enrichment question but rejected zero-enrichment as a precondition. The revised proposal acknowledged some movement toward US positions but maintained core redlines on sovereignty and sanctions relief.

media.caption: Iran submits revised 14-point peace proposal to the US via Pakistan, covering sanctions, Hormuz, and nuclear issues

title: Araghchi Conducts Intensive Shuttle Diplomacy Across Region on Peace Talks
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held separate phone calls with his Saudi Arabian, French, Qatari, Turkish, and South Korean counterparts, seeking to coordinate regional and international support for Iran's peace proposal. He also met with Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Tehran, discussing the structure of indirect US-Iran talks and Iran's conditions for a comprehensive deal — including an end to the naval blockade, sanctions relief, and a nuclear verification mechanism that preserves Iran's enrichment rights. Araghchi also reaffirmed Iran's position that the country's sovereignty must be respected in any settlement and that the pace of negotiations must accelerate given Iran's deteriorating economic situation.

media.caption: FM Araghchi conducts intensive regional shuttle diplomacy to build support for Iran's peace framework
